title: Completion of a strict henselization is Noetherian and faithfully flat
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian local commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, let $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ be its strict henselization with respect to a separable closure of its residue field [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples], and let $\mathfrak m^{\mathrm{sh}}=\mathfrak mR^{\mathrm{sh}}$ be the maximal ideal of $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$. Let $\widehat{R^{\mathrm{sh}}}=\varprojlim_n R^{\mathrm{sh}}/(\mathfrak m^{\mathrm{sh}})^n$ be the completion at this ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Then $\widehat{R^{\mathrm{sh}}}$ is Noetherian and the canonical local map $R^{\mathrm{sh}}\to\widehat{R^{\mathrm{sh}}}$ is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Lemma Tag 06LJ (lemma-henselization-noetherian), proof parts (a) and (c), specialized to the strict henselization

proof.text: Put C=R^{\mathrm{sh}} and I=\mathfrak mC. By the strict henselization triples statement, C is local with maximal ideal I and residue field a separable closure of R/\mathfrak m. Since R is Noetherian, \mathfrak m is finitely generated, hence I is finitely generated; the residue field C/I is Noetherian. Applying the general completion criterion [lem-weil-pbc-completion-noetherian-quotient-noetherian] to (C,I) shows that \widehat C is Noetherian.

source.place: Lemma Tag 06LJ, proof part (a), paragraph beginning 'As m is finitely generated'

proof.text: The canonical map C\to\widehat C is flat by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-completion-flat].

source.place: Lemma Tag 06LJ, proof part (c), paragraph beginning 'To finish the proof of (c)'

proof.text: Locality of $C\to\widehat C$. Let $\pi:\widehat C\to C/I$, $(x_n)_n\mapsto x_1$, and $\iota:C\to\widehat C$ the canonical map, so $\pi\circ\iota$ is the quotient map $C\to C/I$. Each $C/I^n$ is local with nilpotent maximal ideal $I/I^n$ (Step 1: $I$ is the maximal ideal of $C$), so $x_n\in C/I^n$ is a unit iff its image $x_1\in C/I$ is nonzero. Hence if $x=(x_n)\in\widehat C$ has $x_1\ne0$, every $x_n$ is a unit and the inverses are compatible by uniqueness, so $x$ is a unit; the non-units are therefore exactly $\ker\pi$, a proper ideal. Thus $\widehat C$ is local with maximal ideal $\ker\pi$, and $\iota^{-1}(\ker\pi)=\ker(C\to C/I)=I$, so $\iota$ is a local homomorphism.

source.place: Lemma Tag 06LJ, part (a): (R^{sh})^\wedge is a local ring; elementary inverse-limit argument

proof.text: By Step 2 the map $C\to\widehat C$ is flat and by Step 3 it is a local homomorphism of local rings. Therefore it is faithfully flat by the flat-local faithfully-flat lemma [lem-pc-local-flat-faithful-flat-reflects-surjective].
